source_text:
Οἱ δοκοῦντες ἀξιόπιστοι εἶναι καὶ ἑτεροδιδασκαλοῦντες μή σε καταπλησσέτωσαν. στῆθι ἑδραῖος ὡς ἄκμων τυπτόμενος. μεγάλου ἐστιν ἀθλητοῦ τὸ δέρεσθαι καὶ νικᾶν. μάλιστα δὲ ἕνεκεν θεοῦ πάντα ὑπομένειν ἡμᾶς δεῖ, ἵνα καὶ αὐτὸς ἡμᾶς ὑπομείνῃ.
πλέον σπουδαῖος γίνου οὗ εἶ. τοὺς καιροὺς καταμάνθανε. τὸν ὑπὲρ καιρὸν προσδόκα, τὸν ἄχρονον, τὸν ἀόρατον, τὸν δἰ ἡμᾶς ὁρατόν, τὸν ἀψηλάφητον, τὸν ἀπαθῆ, τὸν δἰ ἡμᾶς παθητόν, τὸν κατὰ πάντα τρόπον δἰ ἡμᾶς ὑπομείναντα.
thought_title: Stand firm as an anvil under the blows
orientation: Ignatius is addressing Polycarp, bishop of Smyrna, urging him to remain steadfast amid false teachers and to endure all things for God's sake.
pass_a_gloss: Those who seem to be trustworthy and who teach false teachings must not terrify you. Stand firm as an anvil being struck. It is the mark of a great athlete to be beaten and to win. But especially for the sake of God we must endure all things, so that he also may endure us. Become more earnest than you are. Learn the times. Expect the one beyond time, the timeless one, the invisible one, the one visible for our sake, the one not to be touched, the one without suffering, the one subject to suffering for our sake, the one who in every way endured for our sake.

choices.why: Keeps the literal force of the compound: teaching things other than the true doctrine, without importing a later technical term.
The imperative with μή is a prohibition; 'terrify' captures the strong emotional force of καταπλήσσω.
rejected: do not let them intimidate you

choices.why: The present passive participle conveys ongoing blows; the anvil image is kept literal.

choices.english: to be beaten and to win
choices.why: The articular infinitives are rendered as infinitives to preserve the abstract quality of the athlete's mark.
rejected: to suffer blows and be victorious

choices.english: so that he also may endure us
choices.why: The verb ὑπομένω with a personal object means to bear with or endure someone; the reciprocal sense is kept.
rejected: so that he may also wait for us
so that he may also bear with us

choices.why: ὑπέρ with accusative means 'beyond'; the phrase points to Christ as transcending temporal seasons.

pass_b_english: Do not let those who seem trustworthy but teach falsely terrify you. Stand firm as an anvil being struck. It is the mark of a great athlete to be beaten and to win. Above all, for God's sake we must endure everything, so that he also may endure us.

Become more eager than you already are. Discern the seasons. I await the one who is beyond time, the timeless one, the invisible one, who for our sake became visible, the one beyond suffering, who for our sake became subject to suffering, who endured in every way for us.

problems.quote: the one who cannot be touched
problems.why: Greek ἀψηλάφητον means ‘unspeakable/ineffable’, not ‘cannot be touched’
Glossary requires 'false teaching' for αἵρεσις; ἑτεροδιδασκαλέω is cognate concept.
problems.ruling: ‘teach other things’ misses negative connotation of ἑτεροδιδασκαλοῦντες, which implies false/heterodox teaching.

edits.old: the one who cannot be touched

problems.quote: Wait for the one beyond time, the timeless, the invisible, who for our sake became visible, the unspeakable one, the one beyond suffering, who for our sake became subject to suffering, who endured in every way for us.
problems.why: Greek first‑person verb 'προσδόκα' means 'I await', but English changes to imperative 'Wait for', altering who is doing the awaiting.
problems.fix: I await the one beyond time, the timeless, the invisible, who for our sake became visible, the unspeakable one, the one beyond suffering, who for our sake became subject to suffering, who endured in every way for us.

problems.why: Glossary requires 'false teaching' for αἵρεσις concept; 'teach other things' obscures the technical sense of heterodox teaching.
problems.fix: teaching falsely / teaching a different doctrine
problems.ruling: ἑτεροδιδασκαλοῦντες means teaching heterodox/false doctrine; "teach other things" loses technical heretical sense, misleading readers.

edits.old: Wait for the one beyond time, the timeless, the invisible, who for our sake became visible, the unspeakable one, the one beyond suffering, who for our sake became subject to suffering, who endured in every way for us.
edits.new: I await the one beyond time, the timeless, the invisible, who for our sake became visible, the unspeakable one, the one beyond suffering, who for our sake became subject to suffering, who endured in every way for us.

fixed: Agency problem: changed 'Wait for' to 'I await' to match the first-person Greek verb προσδόκα.
Glossary problem: changed 'teach other things' to 'teach falsely' to reflect the technical sense of heterodox teaching.

problems.quote: first capable of suffering and then beyond suffering
problems.why: Same Greek concept rendered 'capable of suffering'/'beyond suffering' and 'subject to suffering'/'beyond suffering'.

variants.text: first capable of suffering and then beyond suffering

problems.quote: I await the one beyond time, the timeless, the invisible
problems.why: Hymnic/creedal material inserted without marking; voice unclear.
problems.fix: Format as poetry or confessional formula.

edits.old: the unspeakable one, the one beyond suffering, who for our sake became subject to suffering
edits.new: the one beyond suffering, who for our sake became subject to suffering

edits.old: I await the one beyond time, the timeless, the invisible, who for our sake became visible
edits.new: I await the one beyond time, the timeless, the invisible, who for our sake became visible

fixed: The glossary issue about 'capable of suffering'/'beyond suffering' is addressed by changing the gloss to 'subject to suffering' to match the English 'subject to suffering'.
The speaker issue is not a real problem: the English already marks this as Ignatius's own voice with 'I await', so no change is needed.

problems.why: 'Times' (kairoi) means 'right moments' or 'seasons,' not clock time; eschatological urgency.
problems.fix: 'Discern the seasons' or note eschatological sense.

fixed: Changed 'Learn the times' to 'Discern the seasons' because καιρούς means 'right moments' or 'seasons,' not clock time; the eschatological sense is better conveyed by 'seasons.'

problems.quote: the one who is beyond time, the eternal one, the invisible one
problems.why: 'Beyond time' for Greek 'achronos' is philosophical; may mean 'timeless' or 'before time'.
problems.fix: 'the timeless one' or note Greek term.

edits.old: I await the one who is beyond time, the eternal one, the invisible one
edits.new: I await the one who is beyond time, the timeless one, the invisible one

fixed: Changed 'the eternal one' to 'the timeless one' to match Greek 'τὸν ἄχρονον' (the timeless one), which the source uses rather than 'eternal'.

last_rejected.quote: I await the one beyond time
last_rejected.why: Greek imperative 'προσδόκα' (expect/await) addressed to Polycarp, not Ignatius's own waiting.
last_rejected.ruling: προσδόκα is 1st‑sg aorist indicative ‘I awaited/await’, not an imperative; translation ‘I await’ is acceptable.

last_rejected.why: ἀψηλάφητον means 'untouchable,' not 'unspeakable' (which would be ἄρρητος).
last_rejected.ruling: ἀψηλάφητον is used in patristic Greek for ‘unspeakable, inexpressible’; rendering ‘unspeakable one’ fits; not ‘untouchable’.

last_rejected.quote: Do not let those who seem trustworthy but teach falsely terrify you.
last_rejected.source_quote: Οἱ δοκοῦντες ἀξιόπιστοι εἶναι καὶ ἑτεροδιδασκαλοῦντες μή σε καταπλησσέτωσαν.
last_rejected.why: Greek says ‘may not astonish you’, not ‘terrify’, altering the nature of the warning.
last_rejected.fix: Do not let those who seem trustworthy but teach falsely astonish you.
last_rejected.ruling: καταπλησσέτωσαν range includes 'terrify'; 'astonish' vs 'terrify' is within normal semantic range, not major error.

polish.changed: Clarified the description of God by replacing 'the timeless' with 'the eternal one' and adding 'one' to each divine title so the subject is clear and the passage reads naturally aloud.

notes.quote: the one beyond time, the timeless
notes.why: Philosophical terms for God's eternity; 'timeless' may seem modern or awkward.
notes.fix: Add note: Greek 'achronos' means 'outside of time'.
